name: Conor Gunn
highlight: Gunn crossed in 9h11 in 1994, midway through a run of ten consecutive Irish 17 km championship wins.
biography: Conor Gunn was 22 when he crossed from England to France on 2 September 1994. D. Ford piloted Sea Satin, with Joe Gunn listed as trainer. The swim earned the Channel Swimming Association’s award for the fastest swim by a British person that season.

Between 1992 and 2001 Gunn won the Irish men’s 17 km open-water championship ten years in succession. He placed second over 10.5 miles on Windermere in 1993. In 2001 he finished 13th around Manhattan, and in 2020 he entered the Ireland Marathon Swimming Hall of Fame.
